text:
sam.green: Heads up — the nf4+fp4 canary on the small GPU pool just regressed. ~25% throughput drop and per-GPU reserved mem climbs steadily over ~30m. Canary id: canary-2026-03-17-9. Started at ~2267890123.
infra-bot: deploy: canary canary-2026-03-17-9 -> eng-runtime-small started by @sam.green :rocket:
tara.k: What model/variant and exact wave? Any stderr traces yet?
sam.green: Model: gpt-large@v2.3.6 using mixed-quant profile (nf4 primary, fp4 allowed). Canary config: runtime.quant_policy=hybrid, batching.window=100ms. Initial perf sample: baseline 860 req/s -> canary 640 req/s. GPU reserved mem before: ~2.1GB -> after ~5.8GB.
maria: KV cache growth looks suspicious — we see repeated mallocs in kv slab after ~2k requests. Can you paste the short profiling dump?
sam.green: quick pprof dump from the service cpu profile (trimmed):
```
pprof --text /tmp/profile.pb
Total: 1200ms
  cudaMemcpyAsync           340ms  28.3%
  kv_cache_realloc          210ms  17.5%
  nf4_kernel_dispatch       180ms  15.0%
  fallback_slow_path        160ms  13.3%
  batch_prefetch            120ms  10.0%
```
ben: Interesting — cudaMemcpyAsync at top suggests host<->device churn. Any NVTX traces for memcpys?
perf-bot: nvprof snapshot from one slow request (short):
```
GPUMemcpy HtoD  1.2ms x 48 calls
GPUKernel nf4_dispatch 0.9ms x 96 calls
GPUKernel fp4_dispatch 1.6ms x 12 calls
```
ben: Looks like mixed kernel dispatch pattern (a few fp4 kernels interleaved). When dispatcher flips variant mid-request we hit extra memcpy for layout transforms.
derek: I think this is the kernel selector edge-case: quant_profile scoring returns fp4 for some layers (small weight ranges), but the runtime glue isn't using the in-GPU fp4 path — it falls back and does host-side reformat then H2D memcpy. That explains memcpy spikes + kv reallocs (layout mismatch forces new KV buffers).
tara.k: Do we have a log snippet from kernel_selector showing the chosen variant reason?
ben: Copied a runtime snippet from canary logs:
```
[kernel_selector] layer=12 score(fp4)=0.82 score(nf4)=0.79 chosen=fp4 reason=quant_profile_match
[dispatcher] using nf4_dispatch path for layer=12 (missing device-fp4-kernel)
```
maria: So kernel_selector thinks fp4 is best, but device kernel table isn't populated for fp4 for that model shape -> dispatcher does a host-layout transform and uses nf4 kernel. Two-step path.
sam.green: Repro steps I used:
```
curl -X POST https://canary.int.redwood/api/v1/infer -d '{"model":"gpt-large@v2.3.6","input":"hello"}' -H 'x-redwood-canary: canary-2026-03-17-9'
# or run the local runner with --quant-policy=hybrid --runtime.prefetch=on
```
perf-bot: Additional note: batching heuristics interact — when effectivebatch < micro_batch_threshold (16) we enable micro-batching codepath that does per-micro prefetch and sometimes triggers extra KV transfers.
derek: Proposed immediate mitigation: flip runtime flag to disable dynamic kernel selection (force nf4-only) for the canary pool, roll back quant_policy to nf4_strict. That should remove host transform path and KV churn.
tara.k: Longer-term fixes:
 - ship missing device fp4 kernels for the shape(s) hitting fallback
 - add strict validation in kernel_selector: only pick variant if device kernel exists and kv-layout compatible
 - log per-layer selector score+device_availability to trace regressions
maria: I can add a short patch to kernel_selector to emit: layer, scores, chosen, device_table_hit boolean. Small change + unit test.
ben: I'll add a gating flag runtime.kernel_force_variant with values {auto, nf4_only, fp4_only} and expose it to the canary UI. Will target PR today.
derek: I'll bisect dispatcher change that introduced host-transform fallback last month (PR 1227). If we can find the commit that removed the device fp4 registration for certain shapes, we fix the root cause.
sam.green: Action items & owners:
 - ben: gate flag + canary flip (nf4_only) (ETA: 4h)
 - maria: add selector logging + test (ETA: EOD)
 - derek: run bisect on dispatcher/kernel-registration (ETA: 6h)
 - tara.k: monitor mem/reserved after canary flag flip, collect pprof+nvtx (ETA: 6-8h)
 - sam.green: collect traces and confirm perf delta (ETA: after canary)

sam.green: If flag flip restores throughput we keep it for 48h and then ship device fp4 kernels and selector guard.
infra-bot: deploy: canary update applied (runtime.kernel_force_variant=nf4_only) by @ben. Rolling out to pool eng-runtime-small :white_check_mark:
tara.k: After flip — initial quick sample: 820 req/s and reserved mem stable at ~2.2GB. Will keep monitoring.
maria: Logging patch PR created: r/1234. Adds per-layer selector telemetry to /internal/telemetry/selector.
ben: PR for gate submitted r/1235. Attaching to canary. Will coordinate with tara for rollback cadence.
derek: Found candidate regressing commit: r/1227 (device-registry: lazy-register device variants). Investigating whether lazy path skipped fp4 for some dims.
sam.green: Great triage. Thanks everyone. Keep updates in thread — ping me for any blocker. :thumbsup:
